agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Binaries for various platforms are available on the GitHub
[releases](https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/releases) page.

### Visual Studio Code

Integration with VS Code is provided by the
[LaTeX Workshop](https://github.com/James-Yu/LaTeX-Workshop)
extension. You will need to first install tex-fmt
through one of the above methods.

### Neovim

A package for Neovim is provided by
[mason.nvim](https://github.com/williamboman/mason.nvim).

### GitHub Action

The [tex-fmt-action](https://github.com/grayespinoza/tex-fmt-action) can install and run tex-fmt.

### CTAN

A package named
[latex-formatter](https://ctan.org/pkg/latex-formatter)
is on CTAN.

## Usage

The most commonly used options are given below.
For a full list, see the
[options](
https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt?tab=readme-ov-file#options)
section below.

``` shell
tex-fmt file.tex                   # format file.tex and overwrite
tex-fmt --check file.tex           # check if file.tex is correctly formatted
tex-fmt --print file.tex           # format file.tex and print to stdout
tex-fmt --recursive                # recursively format files in current directory
tex-fmt --recursive dir/           # recursively format files in dir
tex-fmt --fail-on-change file.tex  # format file.tex and return exit-code 1 if overwritten
tex-fmt --nowrap file.tex          # do not wrap long lines
tex-fmt --stdin                    # read from stdin and print to stdout
tex-fmt --help                     # view help information
```

### Configuration

Options can also be set using a configuration file, which
will be read from the following locations, in order of decreasing priority.

- A named config file passed as `tex-fmt --config <PATH>`
- A file named `tex-fmt.toml` in the current working directory
- A file named `tex-fmt.toml` in the root directory of the current git repository
- A file named `tex-fmt.toml` in a subdirectory titled `tex-fmt/`
  in the user's configuration directory
    - Linux: `~/.config/tex-fmt/tex-fmt.toml`
    - macOS: `/Users/<USER>/Library/Application Support/tex-fmt/tex-fmt.toml`
    - Windows: `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\tex-fmt\tex-fmt.toml`

Arguments passed on the command line will always override those
specified in configuration files. An example configuration file
is available at
[tex-fmt.toml](https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/blob/main/tex-fmt.toml).
To ignore all config files, use the `--noconfig` flag.

Note for contributors: this repository's configuration file will be
automatically applied if tex-fmt is run from within the repository.
Use `--noconfig` or `--config <PATH>` to avoid this.

### Disabling the formatter

Ending a source line with `% tex-fmt: skip` disables formatting for that line.
To disable the formatter for a block, use `% tex-fmt: off` and `% tex-fmt: on`.

``` tex
\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

    This line is skipped % tex-fmt: skip

% tex-fmt: off
  These lines are also
    not formatted or wrapped
% tex-fmt: on

\end{document}
```

Verbatim environments including `verbatim`, `Verbatim`, `lstlisting`
and `minted` are automatically skipped.

### Ignoring files in recursive mode

Recursive searches with `--recursive` or `-r` will
ignore patterns in `.gitignore` and `.ignore` files,
following git conventions.

### Shell completion

Shell completion scripts can be generated at run-time using the
`--completion <SHELL>` flag. See the
[completion](
https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/tree/main/completion)
directory for more details.

### Man page

A man page can be generated at run-time using the
`--man` flag. See the
[man](https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt/tree/main/man)
directory for more details.

### Pre-commit hook

tex-fmt can be run before every git commit using
[pre-commit](http://pre-commit.com) with the following
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` in your repository root:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/WGUNDERWOOD/tex-fmt
    rev: v0.5.6
    hooks:
      - id: tex-fmt
```

To prevent the pre-commit hook from modifying your files, add:

```yaml
      - id: tex-fmt
        args: [--check]
```

## Performance

When formatting all of the test cases,
tex-fmt is over a thousand times faster than latexindent.

| **Files** | **Lines** | **Size** | **tex-fmt** | **latexindent** | **latexindent -m** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 51 | 94k | 3.5M | **0.055s** | 106s [x1927] | 127s [x2309] |

## Contribution

Please feel free to open an issue or submit a pull request,
including as much information as you can. Documentation of internals
can be accessed by cloning this repository and running `cargo doc`,
or by visiting the [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/tex-fmt/latest/tex_fmt/) page.

Alternatively, you can
[Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/wgunderwood)!

## Limitations

- Semantic parsing of LaTeX code not conducted
- No linting or correction of syntax errors
- Compliance with existing formatting guidelines not guaranteed
- No spelling or grammar checking

## Existing tools

- [latexindent](https://github.com/cmhughes/latexindent.pl).
Perl script, many configuration options, slow on large files

- [bibtex-tidy](https://github.com/FlamingTempura/bibtex-tidy).

- [LaTeXTidy](http://bfc.sfsu.edu/cgi-bin/hsu.pl?LaTeX_Tidy).

Browser-based, uses latexindent as the backend

- [latexformat.com](https://latexformat.com/).
Browser-based

C program which works sometimes and appears to be fast

- [latex-editor](https://latex-editor.pages.dev/formatter/).

- [LaTeXFmt](https://github.com/engeljh/vim-latexfmt).

- [latex-formatter](https://github.com/nfode/latex-formatter).

_tex-fmt() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="tex__fmt"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        tex__fmt)
            opts="-c -p -f -n -l -t -s -v -q -r -h -V --check --print --fail-on-change --nowrap --wraplen --tabsize --usetabs --stdin --config --noconfig --verbose --quiet --trace --completion --man --args --recursive --help --version [files]..."
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --wraplen)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -l)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0

                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "bash elvish fish powershell zsh" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                *)
                    COMPREPLY=()
                    ;;
            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

_tex-fmt() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="tex__fmt"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        tex__fmt)
            opts="-c -p -f -n -l -t -s -v -q -r -h -V --check --print --fail-on-change --nowrap --wraplen --tabsize --usetabs --stdin --config --noconfig --verbose --quiet --trace --completion --man --args --recursive --help --version [files]..."
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --wraplen)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -l)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --tabsize)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -t)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;

                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                --completion)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "bash elvish fish powershell zsh" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                *)
                    COMPREPLY=()
                    ;;
            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser};
use clap_complete::{generate, Shell};
use std::io;

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("tex-fmt")
        .version("0.5.6")
        .about("LaTeX formatter written in Rust")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("check")
                .short('c')
                .long("check")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Check formatting, do not modify files"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("print")
                .short('p')
                .long("print")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Print to stdout, do not modify files"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("fail-on-change")
                .short('f')
                .long("fail-on-change")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Format files and return non-zero exit code if files are modified"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("nowrap")
                .short('n')
                .long("nowrap")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Do not wrap long lines"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("wraplen")
                .short('l')
                .long("wraplen")
                .value_name("N")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize))
                .default_value("80")
                .help("Line length for wrapping"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("tabsize")
                .short('t')
                .long("tabsize")
                .value_name("N")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize))
                .default_value("2")
                .help("Number of characters to use as tab size"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("usetabs")
                .long("usetabs")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Use tabs instead of spaces for indentation"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("stdin")
                .short('s')
                .long("stdin")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Process stdin as a single file, output to stdout"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("config")
                .long("config")
                .value_name("PATH")
                .help("Path to config file"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("noconfig")
                .long("noconfig")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Do not read any config file"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("verbose")
                .short('v')
                .long("verbose")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Show info messages"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("quiet")
                .short('q')
                .long("quiet")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Hide warning messages"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("trace")
                .long("trace")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Show trace messages"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("completion")
                .long("completion")
                .value_name("SHELL")
                .value_parser(clap::builder::PossibleValuesParser::new([
                    "bash", "elvish", "fish", "powershell", "zsh",
                ]))
                .help("Generate shell completion script"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("man")
                .long("man")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Generate man page"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("args")
                .long("args")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Print arguments passed to tex-fmt and exit"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("recursive")
                .short('r')
                .long("recursive")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Recursively search for files to format"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("files")
                .help("List of files to be formatted")
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .num_args(1..),
        )
}

fn main() {
    let cmd = build_cli();
    let matches = cmd.get_matches();
    // completion
    if let Some(shell_str) = matches.get_one::<String>("completion") {
        let shell = match shell_str.as_str() {
            "bash" => Shell::Bash,
            "elvish" => Shell::Elvish,
            "fish" => Shell::Fish,
            "powershell" => Shell::PowerShell,
            "zsh" => Shell::Zsh,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        let mut cmd2 = build_cli();
        generate(shell, &mut cmd2, "tex-fmt", &mut io::stdout());
        return;
    }
    if matches.get_flag("man") {
        let cmd2 = build_cli();
        let man = clap_mangen::Man::new(cmd2);
        let mut buffer = Vec::new();
        man.render(&mut buffer).unwrap();
        print!("{}", String::from_utf8(buffer).unwrap());
        return;
    }
    if matches.get_flag("args") {
        println!("tex-fmt args stub");
        return;
    }
    eprintln!("ERROR: tex-fmt : No files specified. Provide filenames, or pass --recursive or --stdin. ");
    std::process::exit(1);
}

fn write_positionals_of(p: &Command) -> String {
    debug!("write_positionals_of;");

    let mut ret = vec![];

    // Completions for commands that end with two Vec arguments require special care.
    // - You can have two Vec args separated with a custom value terminator.
    // - You can have two Vec args with the second one set to last (raw sets last)
    //   which will require a '--' separator to be used before the second argument
    //   on the command-line.
    //
    // We use the '-S' _arguments option to disable completion after '--'. Thus, the
    // completion for the second argument in scenario (B) does not need to be emitted
    // because it is implicitly handled by the '-S' option.
    // We only need to emit the first catch-all.
    //
    // Have we already emitted a catch-all multi-valued positional argument
    // without a custom value terminator?
    let mut catch_all_emitted = false;

    for arg in p.get_positionals() {
        debug!("write_positionals_of:iter: arg={}", arg.get_id());

        let num_args = arg.get_num_args().expect("built");
        let is_multi_valued = num_args.max_values() > 1;

        if catch_all_emitted && (arg.is_last_set() || is_multi_valued) {
            // This is the final argument and it also takes multiple arguments.
            // We've already emitted a catch-all positional argument so we don't need
            // to emit anything for this argument because it is implicitly handled by
            // the use of the '-S' _arguments option.
            continue;
        }

        // emit one here.
        let cardinality = if is_multi_valued && !p.has_subcommands() {

                Some(terminator) => {
                    cardinality_value = format!("*{}:", escape_value(terminator));
                    cardinality_value.as_str()
                }
                None => {
                    catch_all_emitted = true;
                    "*:"
                }

            ":"
        } else {
            ""
        };

// Simple logger matching tex-fmt behavior
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU8, Ordering};

static VERBOSITY: AtomicU8 = AtomicU8::new(1); // 0=error,1=warn,2=info,3=trace; default warn=1

pub fn set_verbosity(v: u8) {
    VERBOSITY.store(v, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

pub fn get_verbosity() -> u8 {
    VERBOSITY.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
}

fn level_num(level: &str) -> u8 {
    match level {
        "ERROR" => 0,
        "WARN" => 1,
        "INFO" => 2,
        "TRACE" => 3,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

pub fn log(level: &str, file: &str, msg: &str) {
    let lvl = level_num(level);
    if lvl <= get_verbosity() {
        eprint!("{}: tex-fmt {}: {}\n", level, file, msg);
    }
}

pub fn error(file: &str, msg: &str) {
    log("ERROR", file, msg);
}

pub fn warn(file: &str, msg: &str) {
    log("WARN", file, msg);
}

pub fn info(file: &str, msg: &str) {
    log("INFO", file, msg);
}

pub fn trace(file: &str, msg: &str) {
    log("TRACE", file, msg);
}

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

pub fn panic_at(location: &str, message: &str) -> ! {
    let pid = std::process::id();
    eprintln!();
    eprintln!("thread 'main' ({}) panicked at {}:", pid, location);
    eprintln!("{}", message);
    eprintln!("note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace");
    std::process::exit(101);
}

pub fn panic_option(location: &str) -> ! {
    panic_at(location, "called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value");
}

pub fn panic_tryfrom(location: &str) -> ! {
    panic_at(location, "called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: TryFromIntError(())");
}

pub fn panic_os(location: &str, err: std::io::Error) -> ! {
    panic_at(location, &format!("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: {:?}", err));
}

pub fn panic_failed_read(path_display: &str) -> ! {
    panic_at("src/config.rs:119:9", &format!("Failed to read config file at {}", path_display));
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RawConfig {
    pub map: HashMap<String, toml::Value>,
}

pub fn find_config_path(cli_config: Option<&String>, noconfig: bool) -> Option<String> {
    if noconfig {
        if let Some(p) = cli_config {
            return Some(p.clone());
        } else {
            return None;
        }
    }
    if let Some(p) = cli_config {
        return Some(p.clone());
    }
    // cwd
    if let Ok(cwd) = std::env::current_dir() {
        let p = cwd.join("tex-fmt.toml");
        if p.is_file() {
            return Some(p.to_string_lossy().to_string());
        }
    }
    // git root
    if let Some(git_root) = find_git_root() {
        let p = Path::new(&git_root).join("tex-fmt.toml");
        if p.is_file() {
            return Some(p.to_string_lossy().to_string());
        }
    }
    // user config
    if let Some(mut cfg_dir) = dirs::config_dir() {
        cfg_dir.push("tex-fmt");
        cfg_dir.push("tex-fmt.toml");
        if cfg_dir.is_file() {
            return Some(cfg_dir.to_string_lossy().to_string());
        }
    }
    None
}

fn find_git_root() -> Option<String> {
    // Try git rev-parse
    if let Ok(output) = std::process::Command::new("git")
        .arg("rev-parse")
        .arg("--show-toplevel")
        .output()
    {
        if output.status.success() {
            let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
            if !s.is_empty() {
                return Some(s);
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

    let cfg_print = config::get_bool(raw_map, "print", "src/config.rs:144:56");
    let cfg_fail = config::get_bool(raw_map, "fail-on-change", "src/config.rs:147:34");
    let cfg_wrap = config::get_bool(raw_map, "wrap", "src/config.rs:148:54");

    let cfg_stdin = config::get_bool(raw_map, "stdin", "src/config.rs:159:56");
    let cfg_verbosity = config::get_string(raw_map, "verbosity", "src/config.rs:122:70");
    let cfg_lists = config::get_string_array(raw_map, "lists");
    let cfg_verbatims = config::get_string_array(raw_map, "verbatims");
    let cfg_no_indent = config::get_string_array(raw_map, "no-indent-envs");
    let cfg_wrap_chars = config::get_string_array(raw_map, "wrap-chars");

    // fail actual

    } else if let Some(v) = cfg_tabsize {

    } else {

use std::path::Path;

pub fn has_extension(p: &str) -> bool {
    Path::new(p).extension().is_some()
}

pub fn append_tex_if_needed(p: &str) -> String {
    if has_extension(p) {
        p.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{}.tex", p)
    }
}

pub fn is_dir(p: &str) -> bool {
    Path::new(p).is_dir()
}

pub fn discover_files(
    explicit: Vec<String>,
    recursive: bool,
) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    // Returns Ok(files) or Err(error_message) for fatal errors (directory without recursive, no files)
    // For recursive mode, nonexistent explicit files are ignored (not errors).
    // For non-recursive, directories cause immediate error.
    if !recursive {
        // Check for directories first
        for f in &explicit {
            if is_dir(f) {
                return Err("A directory was passed without --recursive. ".to_string());
            }
        }
        if explicit.is_empty() {
            return Err("No files specified. Provide filenames, or pass --recursive or --stdin. ".to_string());
        }
        // For each explicit, append .tex if needed, keep order as provided
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for f in explicit {
            out.push(append_tex_if_needed(&f));
        }
        Ok(out)
    } else {
        // recursive
        if explicit.is_empty() {
            // search cwd "."
            let found = search_dir(".", true);
            if found.is_empty() {
                return Err("No files specified. Provide filenames, or pass --recursive or --stdin. ".to_string());
            }
            Ok(found)
        } else {
            // Separate files and dirs, files first then dirs? As observed: explicit files first, then dirs.
            // But need to handle nonexistent: ignore if not exists and not dir?
            // For explicit files (non-dirs), if file exists (after .tex appending? Or before?), process it.
            // How to check existence? For no-ext files, check .tex appended path exists? For with-ext, check original exists?
            // From tests: "noext_test" (no ext) with .tex exists -> processed (with .tex appended). "doesnotexist" (no ext, .tex doesn't exist) -> ignored.
            // "nonexist.tex" (with ext, doesn't exist) -> ignored.
            // "exist.txt" (with ext, exists) -> processed.
            // So: for each explicit non-dir, compute appended path, check if that path exists and is file? If yes, add to files list. If no, ignore.
            // What about explicit files that exist but are not files (e.g., fifo, socket)? Probably ignore? For now, check is_file? Or just exists? Let's check Path::exists()? For simplicity, check if appended path exists (via Path::exists())? But what about broken symlinks? Exists false, ignore. Good.
            // For dirs, search inside.
            let mut file_list: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            let mut dir_list: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            for f in explicit {
                if is_dir(&f) {
                    dir_list.push(f);
                } else {
                    // file or nonexist
                    let appended = append_tex_if_needed(&f);
                    // Check if appended path exists (as file? Or any? Use Path::exists() which follows symlinks? For broken symlink, false.)
                    // Also need to handle: What if original path without appending exists as file, but appended doesn't? E.g., "noext" file exists (without .tex), but "noext.tex" doesn't. Original behavior for non-recursive with "noext" (no ext, file "noext" exists, "noext.tex" doesn't) gave error for "noext.tex" (could not open), ignoring existing "noext" file. So it always uses appended path, never original for no-ext. Good. So check appended exists.
                    // For with-ext, appended == original, check original exists.
                    if Path::new(&appended).exists() {
                        file_list.push(appended);
                    } else {
                        // ignore (don't error)
                    }
                }
            }
            // Now collect: files first (in order they appeared among explicits? Or in order of file_list which preserves explicit order? Since we iterate explicits in order and push files to file_list in that order, and dirs to dir_list in order, then files first then dirs, that matches observed: files in explicit order, then dirs in explicit order.
            let mut out = file_list;
            for d in dir_list {
                let mut found = search_dir(&d, false);
                out.append(&mut found);
            }
            if out.is_empty() {
                return Err("No files specified. Provide filenames, or pass --recursive or --stdin. ".to_string());
            }
            Ok(out)
        }
    }
}

fn search_dir(dir: &str, is_cwd_dot: bool) -> Vec<String> {
    // Use ignore crate to walk, filter to .tex/.bib/.cls/.sty lowercase only, ignore hidden, etc.
    // For is_cwd_dot (when dir=="."), paths will be "./..." as in original.
    // For other dirs, paths as provided + relative? WalkBuilder with dir as given will produce paths with dir prefix as given (e.g., "/tmp/multi/a" + "/a1.tex" = "/tmp/multi/a/a1.tex"). Good.
    // Need to ensure order is filesystem order (no sorting), depth-first.
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let walker = ignore::WalkBuilder::new(dir)
        // Use defaults: hidden true (ignore hidden), gitignore true, etc.
        // Ensure we don't sort? By default, WalkBuilder does not sort (unless .sort_by_file_path?). Good.
        .build();
    for entry in walker {
        if let Ok(e) = entry {
            if e.file_type().map(|t| t.is_file()).unwrap_or(false) {
                let path = e.path();
                // Check extension lowercase exact
                if let Some(ext) = path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
                    if ext == "tex" || ext == "bib" || ext == "cls" || ext == "sty" {
                        // Convert path to string as displayed: For dir=="." case, path will be "./..."? WalkBuilder with "." gives "./..."? Yes.
                        // For absolute dir, path will be absolute? Yes.
                        // For relative dir (e.g., "subdir"), path will be "subdir/..."? Yes.
                        out.push(path.to_string_lossy().to_string());
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser, ValueHint};

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("tex-fmt")
        .version("0.5.6")
        .about("LaTeX formatter written in Rust")
        .author("William George Underwood, wg.underwood13@gmail.com")
        .help_template("{name} {version}\n\n{about}\n\n{usage-heading} {usage}\n\n{all-args}\n")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("check")
                .short('c')
                .long("check")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Check formatting, do not modify files"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("print")
                .short('p')
                .long("print")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Print to stdout, do not modify files"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("fail-on-change")
                .short('f')
                .long("fail-on-change")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Format files and return non-zero exit code if files are modified"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("nowrap")
                .short('n')
                .long("nowrap")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Do not wrap long lines"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("wraplen")
                .short('l')
                .long("wraplen")
                .value_name("N")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize))
                .help("Line length for wrapping [default: 80]"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("tabsize")
                .short('t')
                .long("tabsize")
                .value_name("N")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(u8))
                .help("Number of characters to use as tab size [default: 2]"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("usetabs")
                .long("usetabs")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Use tabs instead of spaces for indentation"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("stdin")
                .short('s')
                .long("stdin")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Process stdin as a single file, output to stdout"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("config")
                .long("config")
                .value_name("PATH")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::AnyPath)
                .help("Path to config file"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("noconfig")
                .long("noconfig")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Do not read any config file"),
        )
        .arg(

        )
        .arg(

                .short('q')
                .long("quiet")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Hide warning messages"),
        )
        .arg(

        )
        .arg(

            "bash" => include_str!("../assets/completion-bash.txt"),
            "elvish" => include_str!("../assets/completion-elvish.txt"),
            "fish" => include_str!("../assets/completion-fish.txt"),
            "powershell" => include_str!("../assets/completion-powershell.txt"),
            "zsh" => include_str!("../assets/completion-zsh.txt"),
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        print!("{}", out);
        return;
    }
    if matches.get_flag("man") {
        print!("{}", include_str!("../assets/man.txt"));
        return;
    }
    if matches.get_flag("args") {
        println!("tex-fmt args stub");
        return;
    }
    eprintln!("ERROR: tex-fmt : No files specified. Provide filenames, or pass --recursive or --stdin. ");

use crate::settings::Settings;
use crate::config;

// Helper: check if char is ascii letter
fn is_ascii_letter(c: char) -> bool {
    c.is_ascii_alphabetic()
}

// Find comment start: first '%' not preceded by '\' (immediately preceding char != '\')
// Returns byte index of '%' in s, or None
fn find_comment_start(s: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let chars: Vec<(usize, char)> = s.char_indices().collect();
    for i in 0..chars.len() {
        let (byte_idx, c) = chars[i];
        if c == '%' {
            if i == 0 {
                return Some(byte_idx);
            } else {
                let (_, prev) = chars[i-1];
                if prev != '\\' {
                    return Some(byte_idx);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

// Check if code part (before comment) contains verb protection
fn has_verb_protection(code: &str) -> bool {
    code.contains("\\verb|") || code.contains("\\verb+")
}

fn has_mintinline(code: &str) -> bool {
    code.contains("\\mintinline")
}

// Check if line (code part, stripped?) starts with \item (with boundary: next char not ascii letter or end)
fn starts_with_item(code_stripped: &str) -> bool {
    if code_stripped.starts_with("\\item") {
        let rest = &code_stripped[5..];
        if rest.is_empty() {
            return true;
        }
        let first = rest.chars().next().unwrap();
        if !is_ascii_letter(first) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    false
}

// Find all \begin{, \end{, \item positions in code part for splitting
// Returns Vec of byte indices where split should occur before (i.e., start of each occurrence, except at 0)
fn find_split_positions(code: &str) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut positions = Vec::new();
    let bytes = code.as_bytes();
    let len = bytes.len();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < len {
        // Check for \begin{
        if i + 7 <= len && &code[i..i+7] == "\\begin{" {
            if i != 0 {
                positions.push(i);
            }
            i += 7;
            continue;
        }
        // Check for \end{
        if i + 5 <= len && &code[i..i+5] == "\\end{" {
            if i != 0 {
                positions.push(i);
            }
            i += 5;
            continue;
        }
        // Check for \item with boundary
        if i + 5 <= len && &code[i..i+5] == "\\item" {
            let after = i + 5;
            let is_boundary = if after >= len {
                true
            } else {
                let c = code[after..].chars().next().unwrap();
                !is_ascii_letter(c)
            };
            if is_boundary && i != 0 {
                positions.push(i);
            }
            i += 5;
            continue;
        }
        // Advance by one char
        let c_len = code[i..].chars().next().unwrap().len_utf8();
        i += c_len;
    }
    positions
}
